editorial.title: A Challenge Is Not a Verdict
editorial.verdict: Watch the Reel and use AI to surface objections; verify consequential objections before changing an engineering decision.
editorial.thesis: A plausible AI challenge can become another premature stopping point unless the team converts it into tests, sources and accountable review.

claimMap.claim: Early closure when a choice feels defensible, attributed to Perkins.
claimMap.finding: Perkins and colleagues described a makes-sense epistemology; the Reel paraphrases its name and overstates prevalence with every engineer.

claimMap.claim: Architecture reviews may omit contrary evidence, edge cases and tradeoffs.
claimMap.limit: No specific review or measured outcome in Reel.

claimMap.claim: Most people update their view if contrary evidence is presented; AI can surface it.
claimMap.finding: The prevalence and AI-effect claims are unsupported in the Reel.
claimMap.limit: No cited study, architecture review, benchmark or before-after evidence.

claimMap.claim: Ask AI to argue against the decision.
claimMap.finding: Useful candidate-generation step if objections are independently checked.
claimMap.limit: Exploratory AI-role evidence studied a different decision task and does not validate this prompt for engineering reviews.

primarySources.role: 1991 chapter by D. N. Perkins, Michael Farady and Barbara Bushey, pp. 98–100, for makes-sense epistemology.
Exploratory study of AI advisor roles in news-item classification, not architecture reviews.

limits: Automatic local transcript and timing are uncorrected.
